articles.text: TĀNGMǓ: Zài fēijīshang zuòle zhème yìtiān, gǎnjué zěnmeyàng?
TOM: How do you feel after being on a plane all day like this?
LǏ PÍNG: Zhēn bù shūfu, měicì zuò fēijī dōu xiàng shēng bìng yíyàng. Tèbié shi zài fēijīshang huànle shíjiān, báitian biànchéngle hēiyè, hēiyè biànchéngle báitian, tài nánshòu le!

LǏ PÍNG: I don't feel well at all. Every time I take a plane it's like getting ill. Especially with the time change on the plane, daylight turning into night and night turning back into daylight — how uncomfortable!
TĀNGMǓ: Duì le, bù shūfude shíhou yīnggāi hē diǎnr bīngshuǐr. Wǒ qù gěi ni nòng diǎnr bīngshuǐr lai, hǎo bu hǎo?
TOM: Right. You should have some ice water when you don't feel well. I'll go get you some ice water, okay?
LǏ PÍNG: Hǎo shi hǎo, kěshi wǒ shízài hēbuxiàqu le... Suàn le ba, wǒmen liáoliao tiānr, yěxǔ huì hǎo yìdiǎnr.
LǏ PÍNG: Well, okay, but I really couldn't drink any... Forget it, let's just chat and maybe it'll get a little better.
TĀNGMǓ: Zài guò jǐge zhōngtóu nǐ jiù dào jiā le, xiǎng jiā ma?
TOM: Just another few hours and you'll be home. Are you homesick?
LǏ PÍNG: Xiǎng. Zài Měiguo liǎngnián le, yìtiān máng dào wǎn, méiyou xiǎngguo jiā, kěshi xiànzài xiǎngqǐ jiā lai le. Nǐ shuō qíguài bu qíguài?
LǏ PÍNG: Yes. The whole two years I was in America, I was busy all day long and never got homesick, but now here I am feeling homesick. Don't you think that's strange?
TĀNGMǓ: Nà méiyou shénme qíguài. Rén ma, zǒng yào yǒu diǎnr jiātíng guānniàn. Tèbié shi Zhōngguo rén; Zhōngguo rén shi jiǎng xiàoshùnde.

TOM: There's nothing strange about that. People are people! They have to have a sense of attachment to their family. Especially Chinese people; the Chinese put a lot of importance on filial obedience.
LǏ PÍNG: Wǒ juéde zuò fùmǔ shi hěn bù róngyide, háizi yīnggāi xiàoshùn fùmǔ.
LǏ PÍNG: I think that it's very difficult to be parents, so children ought to be filial toward their parents.
TĀNGMǓ: Zhèige xiǎngfǎ shi nǐ fùmǔ jiāo nǐde ma?
TOM: Did your parents teach you that way of thinking?
LǏ PÍNG: Bú shi, shi shèhuì jiāo wǒde. Wǒ mǔqin cónglái bù hé wǒ tán xiàoshùn.
LǏ PÍNG: No, society taught it to me. My mother never talks to me about filial obedience.
TĀNGMǓ: Zhēnde?
TOM: Really?
LǏ PÍNG: Zhēnde. Wǒ dìyīcì zhuàn qiánde shíhou, cái shíwǔsuì. Huí dào jiāli, jiù bǎ kǒudàilide suǒyǒude qián dōu gěi wǒ mǔqin le, hái shuō wǒ yǐhòu yào xiàoshùn māma.
LǏ PÍNG: Really. The first time I made money I was only fifteen. When I got home, I gave all the money I had in my pocket to my mother, and I said that in the future I must be filial toward her.
TĀNGMǓ: Nǐ māma zěnme shuō?
TOM: What did she say?
LǏ PÍNG: Tā kū le. Tā shuō wǒ néng dúlì, néng zài shèhuìshang zuò ge yǒu yòngde rén jiù shi zuì hǎode xiàoshùn. Wǒ gěi tāde qián, tā dōu gěi wǒ mǎichéng shū. Yǐhòu, wǒ jiù gèng yònggōng le.

LǏ PÍNG: She cried. She said that if I could be independent and be a useful person in society that would be the best way to show filial obedience. She used all the money I gave her to buy books for me. After that, I worked even harder.
TĀNGMǓ: Zhēn shi yíwèi hǎo māma.
TOM: She's really a good mother.
LǏ PÍNG: Shì... Wǒ xiě xìn gěi ta, gàosu ta wǒ yào hé yíwèi Měiguo péngyou yìqǐ huílai guò shǔjià, tā hěn gāoxìng. Tā hěn huānyíng nǐ lái.
LǏ PÍNG: Yes, she is... She was very happy when I wrote her telling her that I was going to come back with an American friend for the summer vacation. She's very glad to have you at our house.
KŌNGZHŌNG XIǍOJIĚ: Duìbuqǐ, liǎngwèi xiānsheng, nǐmen yào hē diǎn shénme?
STEWARDESS: Excuse me, what would you two gentlemen like to drink?
LǏ PÍNG: Wǒ bú dà shūfu, bú yào shénme.
LǏ PÍNG: I'm not feeling too well, I don't want anything.
KŌNGZHŌNG XIǍOJIĚ: Ou, bú dà shūfu? Yìbēi rè chá, hǎo bu hǎo?
STEWARDESS: Oh, you don't feel well? How about a cup of hot tea?
LǏ PÍNG: Hǎode, xièxie ni.
LǏ PÍNG: All right, thank you.
TĀNGMǓ: Wǒ lái yìpíng píjiǔ. Nǐmen yǒu méiyou Heineken?
TOM: I'd like a beer. Do you have Heineken?
KŌNGZHŌNG XIǍOJIĚ: Yǒu.
STEWARDESS: Yes.
TĀNGMǓ: Xièxie.
TOM: Thank you.
KŌNGZHŌNG XIǍOJIĚ: Bú kèqi. Liǎngwèi xiānsheng, nǐ hái yào shénme, qǐng gàosu wo.
STEWARDESS: You're welcome. Sirs, if you want anything else, please let me know.
TĀNGMǓ: Wǒmen shuō dào nǎr le? Duì le, nǐmen jiāli chúle nǐ fùmǔ hé zǔmǔ yǐwài hái yǒu shénme rén ma?
TOM: Now, where were we? Oh yes: is there anyone else in your family besides your parents and your grandmother?
LǏ PÍNG: Nǐ wàngle, wǒ hái yǒu yíge mèimei, zài yínháng zuò shìde.
LǏ PÍNG: You've forgotten that I also have a younger sister who works in a bank.
TĀNGMǓ: Ou, duì le, nǐ gēn wǒ shuōguo, wǒ zěnme wàngle ne!
TOM: Oh, of course. You told me before. How could I have forgotten!

LǏ PÍNG: Shuōdào wǒ mèimei, jiù xiǎngdào wǒ mǔqin. Nǐ zhīdao zài Zhōngguó, zhòng nán qīng nǚde guānniàn háishi yǒude. Kěshi wǒ mèimei shi líkāi dàxué yǐhòu yòu zài Yīngguó niànle liǎngnián shū cái zuò shìde. Zhèi yě yào gǎnxiè wǒ mǔqin.

LǏ PÍNG: Mentioning my sister reminds me of my mother again. You know, in China people still have the concept that men are superior to women. But after my sister graduated from college, she studied for two more years in England before she started working. That was also thanks to my mother.
TĀNGMǓ: Nǐ mèimei xiànzài zhǐ zuò shì, háishi yě niàn diǎnr shū?
TOM: Does your sister just work now, or does she also take some classes?

LǏ PÍNG: Tā zhǐ zuò shì. Búguò tā hěn rèxīn yánjiū dàlùde qíngxing, cháng kàn hěn duō guānyú dàlùde shū. Tā cháng shuō, "Wǒ shi Zhōngguo rén, dàlùshang yǒu shíyì Zhōngguo rén, wǒ zěnme kěyi bù zhīdào tāmende shēnghuó, gōngzuò, hé xuéxíde qíngkuàng ne?"

LǏ PÍNG: She's just working, but she studies the mainland situation very enthusiastically. She reads a lot of books about the mainland. She often says, "I'm Chinese, and there are one billion Chinese on the mainland. How can I be ignorant of the way they live, work, and study?"
TĀNGMǓ: Tāde huà hěn yǒu dàolǐ.
TOM: What she says is quite right.
LǏ PÍNG: Tā yǒu hěn duō dàlù láide péngyou; nǐ hé tā tántan, yě huì juéde hěn yǒu yìsi.
LǏ PÍNG: She has a lot of friends from the mainland; you'll find it very interesting to talk with her.
TĀNGMǓ: Tā duì dàlùde qíngxing zhème rèxīn, nǐ mǔqin yǒu shénme kànfǎ ma?
TOM: Does your mother have anything to say about her enthusiastic interest in the situation on the mainland?
LǏ PÍNG: Tā cháng shuō: "Háizi zhǎngdàle, tāmen yào zǒu shénme lù yīnggāi zìjǐ kǎolǜ."
LǏ PÍNG: She often says, "When children grow up, they should decide for themselves what road they want to take."
TĀNGMǓ: Zhēn hǎo, shízài shi tài hǎo le.
TOM: That's great! That's really wonderful.
LǏ PÍNG: Děng dào nǐ jiàndào tāde shíhou, nǐ yídìng huì xǐhuan ta, yě huì xǐhuan wǒmen jiāde.
LǏ PÍNG: When you meet her I'm sure you'll like her, and our home, too.
TĀNGMǓ: Yídìng!
TOM: I'm sure I will, too!
